name: Clear Terms Studio
summary: A proposal identity organized around the decision, deliverable and acceptance conditions a client must understand.

palette.name: Background
palette.evidence: Native Office page/sheet white ground; explicit design choice retaining the reading surface.

palette.name: Text
palette.evidence: used style Normal explicit text color

typography.usage: Titles and short section openings; source used style Title.
Reading text, supporting labels and detailed explanations; source used style Title.

recognitionRules: Place the proposal identifier, version and date above the title.
Use numbered decision-and-terms sections with clear text tables.
Keep scope, responsibility and acceptance criteria visually separate.
Use black typography and generous table spacing to make commitments inspectable.

principles: Name the choice, its owner and the condition that makes it complete.
Use the identity’s sample as a rhythm and vocabulary reference, not as a factual project claim.
voice.sample: Here is the work, the boundary and what completion will look like.
voice.sampleStatus: Original fictional brand copy authored for this guide, not a quotation or factual claim.
avoid: Avoid certainty about forecasts, capacity or commitments that are still provisional.
Avoid invented testimonials, performance claims and quotation attribution.
voice.secondaryExample: This is the assumption; this is the decision it affects.
voice.cadence: Short opening, concrete follow-through; vary sentence length for explanation.

logoDirection: Use CLEAR TERMS STUDIO in bold Arial with a small monospaced proposal number. No signature flourish or seal.
invariants: Place the proposal identifier, version and date above the title.
Use numbered decision-and-terms sections with clear text tables.
Keep scope, responsibility and acceptance criteria visually separate.
adaptations: Short proposals can collapse sections but must retain deliverables and acceptance.
Long scopes move detailed inventories to an appendix.
Keep the full name with any new symbol until the audience can recognize it independently.

fonts.sourceFontDependency: Arial is a separately licensed Microsoft/system font; not bundled.
Arial is a separately licensed Microsoft/system font; not bundled.

clearSpaceRule: Keep one half of the main wordmark cap height clear around the full silhouette, including its source-derived supporting device.

minimumSize.status: production minimum based on rendered 220/180px wordmark and 32/64px symbol inspection; verify again for unusual substrates
